mechanisms.name: Strict path-type validation (#11819), the main risk
mechanisms.mechanism: 1.12.0 turns `strict-validate-path-type` on by default, and nothing in `values.yaml` or `values-prod.yaml` overrides it, so it applies here. If upstream's path-character validation for `Exact`/`Prefix` rejects `/.well-known` (it starts with a dot segment): with the admission webhook enabled and `--patch-failure-policy=Fail`, the `docs` Ingress would be refused at the next Argo sync or update. It is also unclear whether an existing Ingress is dropped from the generated config when the new controller starts; if so, that would be an outage rather than a refused sync. If `/.well-known` were dropped, security.txt and other RFC 8615 documents would fall through to `docs-site` and return 404. This would be quiet, because the main docs site would keep working.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: From memory, dots, hyphens and underscores are allowed, so `/.well-known` should pass. This is unverified: it could not be confirmed from the supplied documents because the changelog doesn't give the regex. Stopgap, only if the path is rejected: set `strict-validate-path-type: "false"` in `values.yaml`, not pre-emptively.
assumptions: From memory, upstream validation allows dots, hyphens and underscores, so `/.well-known` should pass (unverified)
missingEvidence: The exact path regex behind `strict-validate-path-type` (the changelog doesn't give it)
Whether an existing Ingress is dropped from the generated config when the new controller starts
recommendedValidation: Dry-run the actual Ingress against a 1.12.0 controller in a non-prod cluster with the same values. Apply `apps/docs`, confirm admission accepts it, and confirm `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/` both return 200 from the right backends
Start the 1.12.0 controller with the Ingress already present. Check the controller logs for rejected-Ingress messages and check the generated `nginx.conf` for the `/.well-known` location
Look at the controller source or docs for the exact path regex. Only if it rejects the path, set `strict-validate-path-type: "false"` as a stopgap
